cands.name: Brent Comer

money.note: Covers January 2023 on, primary and general. Party-committee lines are often in-kind staff and mail.

cands.bio: Republican candidate for Alabama State Senate District 28. Raised on a farm in Glennville, Russell County. Has worked about 20 years as a professional landman in oil, gas and energy, and co-owns C & S Bagging and East Alabama Vending in Eufaula. Has held no elected office.
cands.gaps: We found no record of Brent Comer holding elected office. We found no stated positions from him on data centers, homestead property taxes, limits on foreign or investor land buying, growth limits, immigration or H-1B, guns, abortion, school vouchers, or police pay. He did not complete Ballotpedia's 2026 Candidate Connection survey. Ballotpedia lists no endorsements for him. His birthplace and the year he came to or lived in Alabama as an adult are not given. We found no news reporting about him, so no controversies are documented. His job history and business ownership rest only on his own campaign site, with no independent confirmation.

cands.bio: William M. "Billy" Beasley, born 1940, is a pharmacist and businessman from Clayton, Alabama. He graduated from Auburn University in 1962 and ran Clayton Drug Company, Clio Drug Company and Louisville Drug Store. He served in the Alabama House (District 84) from 1998 to 2010. He has been a state senator for District 28 since 2010 and was Senate minority leader from 2017 to 2019.
cands.gaps: We could not find where Beasley was born or raised, or when he came to Alabama. We found no bills he sponsored (the sponsored-legislation table on his Ballotpedia page was empty), and no stated positions or documented actions on data centers, property taxes, land ownership, growth, immigration, policing, guns, abortion or schools. He did not complete Ballotpedia's candidate survey in 2022 or 2026. The only endorsements found were voter-guide recommendations from small groups, which we did not treat as notable. We found no controversies or foreign ties in the pages we had.
